lead: Pregnancy is suspected from the history, confirmed by hCG, and its site, number and age are set by ultrasound. Consider it in every woman of reproductive age with amenorrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain or bleeding, and exclude it before X-rays, teratogenic drugs and surgery.
f: Presumptive (noticed by the woman): amenorrhoea (first and most useful), nausea from about 6 wk, breast tenderness, frequency, tiredness · Quickening at 18–20 wk in a first pregnancy, 16–18 wk later · Probable (found by the examiner): positive hCG, Hegar's sign (soft isthmus, 6–10 wk), Goodell's (soft cervix), Chadwick's (bluish vagina, about 8 wk), Piskacek's (asymmetric uterus), ballottement · Positive (proof): fetal heart on TVS from 6 wk, Doppler from about 12 wk, Pinard from about 24 wk; fetal parts and movements felt by the examiner; fetus seen on scan

sc: Soft isthmus, the fingers almost meet → Hegar's sign
One cornu of the uterus larger → Piskacek's sign

f: Stress, weight loss, heavy exercise, breastfeeding, PCOS, thyroid disease, high prolactin, DMPA, menopause · Bleeding does not exclude pregnancy: implantation bleed, threatened miscarriage, ectopic · Pseudocyesis: firm belief of pregnancy, hCG negative, empty uterus; often linked to infertility: explain gently, counselling

sc: Breastfeeding, 10 wk amenorrhoea, positive test → Pregnant: arrange a dating scan

f: Made by the syncytiotrophoblast; keeps the corpus luteum · Tests measure the β-subunit (α is shared with LH, FSH, TSH) · Serum positive 8–11 days after conception; peak about 100 000 IU/L at 8–10 wk · Viable pregnancy: rises ≥ 35% in 48 h (about doubles) · Urine positive at about the missed period; early-morning urine best; stays positive 2–4 wk after a loss · High: molar, multiple, wrong dates, Down syndrome · Low or not rising: ectopic or failing pregnancy · False negative: too early, dilute urine, hook effect

sc: hCG rises only 20% in 48 h with pain → Ectopic pregnancy
Very high hCG, severe vomiting, uterus large for dates → Molar pregnancy

f: TVS sees each structure about 1 wk before an abdominal scan · Gestational sac 4.5–5 wk: not proof alone (pseudosac of ectopic) · Yolk sac 5–5.5 wk: first definite proof of an intrauterine pregnancy · Fetal pole with heartbeat 6 wk: viable · CRL ≥ 7 mm without heartbeat: missed miscarriage, confirmed by a second opinion or repeat scan ≥ 7 days later · Early scan gives site, viability, number and chorionicity (best before 14 wk), dating, anomalies and NT at 11–14 wk · Discriminatory zone: hCG ≥ 2000 IU/L should show an intrauterine sac on TVS (about 6000 abdominally)

sc: hCG 3500 IU/L, empty uterus on TVS → Ectopic until proven otherwise

f: Expected date of delivery and dating

Gestation counts from the first day of the LMP; term = 280 days · Naegele's rule: LMP + 7 days + 9 months (LMP 10 Jan 2026 → EDD 17 Oct 2026) · Longer cycle: add the extra days (35-day cycle: +7) · LMP unreliable (unsure, irregular, pill or DMPA in the last 3 months, breastfeeding, early bleeding): date by scan · CRL at 11–14 wk: ± 5 days; head at 14–20 wk ± 7–10 days; third trimester ± 3 wk (not for dating) · Scan and LMP differ by more than 5 days: use the scan · Never re-date after a reliable early scan: a small fetus later is growth restriction

sc: First scan at 34 wk shows a small baby → Do not re-date: assess growth

f: First trimester to 13⁺⁶ wk; second 14–27⁺⁶; third from 28 wk · Loss before 24 wk = miscarriage; after = stillbirth · Preterm under 37 wk: extremely preterm under 28, very preterm 28–31⁺⁶, moderate to late 32–36⁺⁶ · Term 37–41⁺⁶: early term 37–38⁺⁶, full term 39–40⁺⁶, late term 41–41⁺⁶ · Post-term 42 wk or more

From about 20 wk the SFH in cm ≈ weeks · First step in any mismatch: check the dates · Larger than dates: multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, molar pregnancy, fibroids, ovarian mass, full bladder · Smaller than dates: FGR, oligohydramnios, IUFD, missed miscarriage, transverse lie, deeply engaged head · Late booking with unknown LMP: combine quickening (add 20–22 wk in a first pregnancy, 22–24 wk later), earliest fundal height and first scan; record the dates as uncertain
